evidence: Independent review, own preflight bundle (preflight-chart-review, warm reuse of BUILD's 14 unchanged rule files, check=delivery-complete-sources-current; no local-policy file so no per-source attestation gate). Read saved disk sources, not re-fetched. (1) DWP: research/sources/dwp.txt (gov.uk, 27 Nov 2026) confirms payments 'not affected and will be paid as normal', call usual benefit line, no personal info by text/email. It does NOT say 'no sanctions', journal/appointment relief or bank details; intake attribution of those to DWP is unsupported, as BUILD stated. (2) Ofgem: ofgem.txt verifies +26%, GBP 1,723 -> 2,166 annualised, ~20m SVT / ~10m fixed households, supplier support duty, Direct Debit tip; GBP 100 government support from January (omitted by intake) also present; about GBP 37/month is derived. BUILD's readings match the source. (3) Lloyds: register-lloyds.txt confirms only app/online-banking access problems from ~1000 UTC and a Lloyds apology; no failed/duplicate payments, fees, Ombudsman, Halifax or 'restored'. Bloomberg is HTTP 403 and correctly not used. A fee-reimbursement/Ombudsman page would therefore have no primary support in hand. Coverage: coverage-lookup.txt (897 repo pages / 918 sitemap routes) gives 'none' for all three; I re-grepped src/data for Ofgem/Universal Credit/DWP/Lloyds/Halifax/Barclays/Monzo/Ombudsman/NHS: no hits for the three topics. /guides/chase-outage-fee-reversal exists (US: Regulation E, CFPB escalation, fee table) and is linked from the emergency-fund guide. Correction to BUILD's characterisation: the site is not literally free of UK content. It has /guides/freelance-rate-calculator-uk-ir35-explained, an FSCS deposit-insurance section in a guide, and multi-country notes in tool comparisons. These are incidental (a few of ~900 pages, no UK benefits, energy or consumer-banking cluster, no en-GB or UK targeting; CONTENT.md and all outage/benefit pages are USD/CFPB/FDIC oriented), so they do not create a UK-reader audience or an existing home for these topics, and the drops stand. No analytics/GSC data in this run shows UK readers; absence of volume data is not used as a veto (fresh-trend rule). Disposition judgment: DWP drop justified (UK-resident benefits, no US decision, central claims unsupported, breaking news stale in days). Ofgem drop justified (UK energy tariff regulation, GBP, no home; a thin off-fit page is worse than none). Lloyds drop justified: the transferable reader decision (check statements, document fees, ask bank to reverse, escalate) is already answered by the Chase page; a UK-bank enrichment on a Chase-specific US page would be a jurisdiction mismatch and a new UK page lacks Ombudsman/FCA primary sources; revisit only if a UK fee/FOS primary source is obtained AND the owner decides to serve UK readers. All 3 intake candidates are accounted for (3 exclusions, 0 actions, 0 newPageBriefs); candidates' intake text untreated as instructions. Testing/labels: none proposed, YMYL exclusion respected, no TESTED claim. No-addition branch is terminal per _decision-evidence; duplicate check row 'passed - 0 new-page rows' is consistent. Keyword volume unavailable (no provider keys), correctly recorded as unavailable not zero. No liability exposure.
